layout_notes: This guide is built for 13CW from three sources: Driver Mod's written 13CW guide (primary), Boosted Films' CW13 Track Tips video, and Full Throttle Driving Academy's CW tutorial for technique depth on the shared corners.

FTDA's video was recorded on configuration 1 CW, which replaces the Sweeper with Star Mazda — its Star Mazda material is deliberately NOT used for zone 7. The Sweeper content comes from Driver Mod and Boosted, who agree it drives as a double apex despite being drawn as a single late apex.
Sunset's apex dip is disputed between sources: FTDA uses it for grip, Driver Mod warns it unsettles the car and bends wheels. Flagged in zone 9 rather than resolved.

1.character: Turn 1, banked to the inside with a fairly early apex. The road drops into a banked pocket mid-corner where grip comes to you, then crests and falls off-camber on exit, so traction disappears just as you want throttle. The braking-zone curb is slippery — braking on it slows the car worse than the pavement beside it. Driver Mod adds that the decreasing radius is what makes the corner work: brake as late as the car allows and you are back on throttle just after turn-in, building progressively (about a fifth throttle at the apex first) — full throttle too early steps the rear out. Boosted's real-track brake reference is the access road on the right, and both video sources say the corner is faster than it looks.

tips: Brake straight beside the curb, not on it

2.character: A low-traction patchwork right-hander climbing a hill — the narrator calls it a mess of a corner. You approach at full throttle and arc gently in; hitting the left curb under braking bounces the car and wrecks braking performance. Brake lightly while still angled, straighten the hands as pressure builds, then threshold-brake at the curb and ride the right curb uphill. Overshooting means too much steering angle and no throttle for the straight after, so rotation must be finished early. Driver Mod brakes from the kink on the approach and puts the car on the inside curbing, where extra camber and a different asphalt patch give grip if you hit it just right; his cue is feeling the suspension set, then getting on throttle before the camber changes — the exit is the hardest acceleration anywhere on the lap.
2.name: Off Ramp

3.character: Entry to the Cotton Corners complex. The video treats Cotton Corners as three linked turns (right, left, uphill right); the sim map has two zones, so this zone carries the first turn and the sequence principle: sacrifice the first two corners to maximise the third corner's exit. Full threshold braking, angle in and clip the curb, but deliberately do not track all the way out — hold mid-track for what follows. Driver Mod's read agrees: in this complex only the entry and the exit matter, and the entry starts with braking early off the I-5 straight so the first turn-in doesn't push wide.
3.name: Cotton Corners 1

4.character: The payoff half of the Cotton Corners complex. Stay left after the middle corner — tracking out here ruins the final turn. Use the whole of the wide inside curb (the fast line kicks up dirt there), then late-apex the uphill right by the flag station and feed the throttle down the hill: one of the fastest acceleration zones on the track. The exit curb is slippery and dusty; run parallel to it rather than on it. Driver Mod works the middle corner with a brief throttle then a touch of left-foot brake to rotate the car without tracking out, and is back on throttle up the hill.

5.character: A long, very fast right-hander (around 100 mph even in a slow car). Enter aimed at an angle from Bus Stop's exit, using the black-marked entry curb under your right-side tyres as the reference. Understeer builds through the corner — manage it with a lift or a light brake drag. The grip lives about a third of the way in from the right edge; further left is marbles and less grip. The second apex is a trap: it sits in a bowl with a divot that unloads the car at speed, so pass a few feet away from it and keep the car flat. Driver Mod calls the apex deceptively late and the corner a maintenance-throttle one — minimum speed is the metric to watch, and never lift fully: if it goes, go off in a straight line rather than saving it. Boosted warns the very inside is bumpy enough to throw the car off and prefers mid-track where it is smoother; both argue against pinching the extreme inside. On exit the corner pushes you left, but Phil Hill needs you on the right — give up a little exit speed to cross back over.

6.character: Steep uphill threshold-braking zone — the hill itself helps scrub speed, so brake as late and hard as the car allows, just shy of ABS. The car goes very light over the crest and, done right, drifts in a neutral four-wheel slide over the top. Turning in late or missing the apex curb delays throttle badly, and exit speed is everything: from the crest it is full throttle down the hill and through the following left kink. Driver Mod stresses the apex is blind: turn in just late enough to line the exit up in a straight line and get on throttle just after the crest — the overshoot here is famous enough that the run-off beyond it is called the splitter graveyard.

7.character: The big outer loop after Phil Hill — the corner the old guide's source video never drove (its layout took Star Mazda instead). You arrive flat out down the hill past the crest kink. The exit is the whole point: it feeds the run through the Esses, and both sources rank it among the most valuable on the lap — giving up a little entry speed pays extremely large dividends on the exit. The line is usually drawn as one long late apex, but both sources drive it as a double apex: an early first apex, let the car drift out to the very edge of the track, then a late second apex and full throttle toward the Esses. Brake very late and use the corner's full width as the braking zone; once turned in, the job is rotating the car so the throttle can go down and stay down. The outer edge ends in sand — dip a wheel off and it spins — so the drift out to the edge is a precision target, not a suggestion.
7.name: Sweeper

8.character: Fast, flowing esses that are full throttle pretty much all the way through until the fourth S — straighten them out and use plenty of curb, with a slight lift at the fourth before getting back on it. Late-apex the last S; it is the trickiest and the dangerous one: going off there can bounce the car back across the track toward the wall at speed. If it goes, straighten the hands and take it straight off to the right into the desert instead of trying to save it. Driver Mod adds that the curbs grow larger the further down you go, and that in a fast car the final kink may not be flat — it can push the car off the right edge. Boosted's S2000 stayed flat all the way through with a smooth wheel, so treat flat as car-dependent.
8.name: Esses

tips.text: Flat out until the fourth S

9.character: Final corner onto the main straight, and exit speed sets your trap speed at start/finish. Threshold-brake to a mid apex and drop into the divot, where traction comes back; the exit then loses grip again and gets slippery on the rumble strip, so the throttle must be feathered even while you track all the way out and use the strip. Sources disagree on that apex dip: FTDA uses it for grip, while Driver Mod warns the dip unsettles the car and bends wheels and says stay out of it nine times out of ten — treat it as suspect until your own laps say otherwise. Driver Mod also ranks Sunset the lap's biggest PB-killer, mostly through head games: brake a touch early, stay calm, throttle at the apex. And if you overshoot, go off in a straight line — fighting it back loses the rear toward the pit wall. Boosted adds a late apex and warns to keep the right wheel off the entry curbing under braking; it is slippery and pitches the car sideways.
